roleContext.jobDescription: One customer, one record: the customer data platform merges the company's customer records for its marketing and support products, and every change to the merge rules or the consent flags shows up on a product manager's screen. The engineer joining the platform team works on merge rules and consent handling from the data product managers' design notes, ships behind a canary, sits down with the marketing and support product managers before each rollout to show them what will change on their screens, and writes the boundary of every change into its pull request. Rollouts go ahead on the platform lead's approval. Reports to the platform lead; works with the data product managers, the privacy team and the platform SRE group.

requirements.text: Works on the merge rules and the consent flags from the data product managers' design notes under the platform engineering standard.
Shows the marketing and support product managers what will change on their screens before each rollout, under the rollout communication standard.
Ships each change behind a canary with the canary result recorded.
Gets the platform lead's approval for each rollout and records which checks were own.
Writes the boundary of every change and its hand-over conditions into the pull request.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Software Engineer, Customer Data Platform

## Experience

- Customer data platform engineer at a marketing software company for three years, building merge-rule and consent-flag changes from the data product managers' design notes under the platform engineering standard; thirty-nine pull requests merged in my name.
- Sat down with the marketing and support product managers before each rollout under the rollout communication standard, showing them what would change on their screens; each pull request links the session note and the product managers' acknowledgement.
- Shipped every change behind a canary, with the canary result attached to the pull request before the rollout.
- Rollouts went ahead on the platform lead's approval, recorded on the pull request with the checks that were mine listed separately.
- The boundary of every change and what the next engineer needs to know are written into the pull request description.

## Work samples

- Work sample: three pull requests with session notes, acknowledgements, canary results and the lead's approval, with the repository references as a verification trail.
